title: Loop host contracts
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and let $I$, $S$, $A$, and $O$ be predicates or functions on Boolean words, with $S(x)$ the initial auxiliary word. Suppose $F$ computes the binary representation of $R(|x|)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps on every input $x$; $I(x,S(x))$ holds, and $I(x,s)$ implies $I(x,S_1(x,s))$ for every $x,s$, where $S_1$ is the state update. Suppose also that each input has a run of $B$ from its initial configuration to the seam configuration in state $a$ with tape words given by $S(x)$, taking at most $T(|x|)$ steps and never visiting state $a$ earlier. For every $x,s$ with $I(x,s)$, suppose there is a positive time at most $T(|x|)$ at which a run from the seam configuration in state $a$ either halts with output $O(x,s)$ when $A(x,s)$ holds, or returns to the seam configuration with updated word $S_1(x,s)$ when $A(x,s)$ fails; in either case it does not visit state $a$ at any strictly intermediate positive time. Then there is a constant $c$ such that, for every input $x$, the loop host has a computation sequence $(C_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}$ and a startup time at most $c(T(|x|)+1)$ with the following properties: the host run from its initial configuration reaches $C_0$ at that startup time, and $C_i$ has empty output for every $i\le R(|x|)$. The configuration $C_{R(|x|)+1}$ is halted and its output is empty in find mode and the one-bit word $[\mathrm{false}]$ otherwise. For each $i\le R(|x|)$ there is a time at most $c(T(|x|)+1)$ such that, if $A(x,S_1^{[i]}(x))$ holds, the host run from $C_i$ halts with output $O(x,S_1^{[i]}(x))$ in find mode and $[\mathrm{true}]$ otherwise; if it fails, that run reaches exactly $C_{i+1}$. At each $C_i$ for $i\le R(|x|)$, every work-tape head lies between $-T(|x|)$ and $T(|x|)$; at the final configuration, every work-tape head lies between $-(T(|x|)+c(T(|x|)+1))$ and $T(|x|)+c(T(|x|)+1)$. Here $S_1^{[i]}$ denotes $i$-fold iteration of the state update.
